query: For eutectic high-entropy alloys intended for structural applications, what single intervention could simultaneously increase strength and ductility? Formulate one testable hypothesis specifying the intervention, its proposed mechanism, the expected improvement relative to an appropriate baseline, the conditions under which it should hold, prior evidence supporting it, and an experiment that could falsify it.

generation.hypothesis: Applying a controlled low‐temperature annealing (aging) treatment to precipitate coherent L12 nano‐precipitates within the fcc lamellae of a eutectic HEA will simultaneously increase the alloy’s strength via precipitation strengthening and preserve (or even slightly enhance) ductility by maintaining effective dislocation storage at lamellar interfaces.
generation.material_initial_state: An as‐cast eutectic high-entropy alloy with a lamellar microstructure composed of soft fcc (or fcc + disordered L12 precursor) and hard B2 (or B2 + bcc) phases.
generation.intervention: Low‐temperature heat treatment (annealing/aging) tailored to precipitate ordered, coherent L12 nano-precipitates within the fcc phase.
generation.conditions: Ambient temperature tensile testing (quasi‐static strain rate of ~10^−3 s^−1) in alloys produced in the as‐cast state; the treatment is applied under conditions (e.g., around 580 °C for an appropriate duration) that enhance L12 formation without causing significant coarsening or loss of lamellar morphology.
generation.structural_mediator: The emergence of coherent L12 precipitates in the fcc lamellae and the formation of precipitate-free soft channels near lamellar interfaces, which together modify the dislocation dynamics.
generation.mechanism: The coherent L12 precipitates act as effective obstacles to dislocation motion (providing precipitation strengthening) while the preservation of the lamellar structure and the maintenance of precipitate-free channels at interfaces allow for high dislocation storage and a self‐generated crack-arresting mechanism, thereby supporting ductility.
generation.predicted_outcome: An increase in yield and ultimate tensile strength (on the order of ~200–300 MPa improvement, as seen in related studies) with only minor (∼2% or less) reductions or even maintained levels of elongation compared to the untreated alloy.
generation.baseline: The as-cast eutectic HEA exhibiting a lamellar fcc + B2 (or fcc + B2 with nano-scale bcc features) microstructure with established strength–ductility metrics.
generation.boundary: This effect is expected under quasi-static loading conditions and may be most effective when the annealing parameters are optimized to control precipitate size and distribution; its performance at very high strain rates or temperatures beyond moderate service conditions remains to be established.
generation.uncertainty: The precise balance between increased strength and retained ductility may be sensitive to the heat-treatment parameters and the resulting precipitate distribution; variations in alloy composition or processing history could lead to deviations from the predicted improvement.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two sets of eutectic HEA samples in the as-cast condition. Subject one set to a controlled low-temperature aging treatment (e.g., 580 °C for 24 hours) to promote coherent L12 precipitate formation, while maintaining the other set as untreated. Characterize both sets using microscopy (TEM/STEM) to confirm lamellar morphology and precipitate distribution, and perform tensile tests under quasi-static conditions.
measurements: Yield strength and ultimate tensile strength (MPa)
Microscopic analysis of precipitate size, coherency, and distribution
Dislocation density and interface characteristics in the fcc lamellae
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the aged (L12-precipitated) samples do not exhibit a statistically significant increase in strength (e.g., ~200–300 MPa improvement) accompanied by at least comparable ductility (within ±2% of elongation) relative to the as-cast samples, or if the heat treatment degrades the lamellar integrity leading to brittle behavior, then the hypothesis is falsified.

The underlying origin lying behind the observed mechanical response is the inherited lamellar geometry from the as-cast EHEA. It is known that grain refinement to the nano/ultrafine-grained regime can render material stronger, but this process is usually accompanied by a dramatic loss of ductility. However, with a composite lamellar architecture, the ultrafine-grained duplex microstructure in this study achieves an improved strength–ductility synergy. Phase decomposition is applied to optimize properties instead of just being a phase-instability phenomenon frequently observed in single-phase HEAs, which may encourage further research in this area. Recent studies indicate that eutectic high-entropy alloys can simultaneously possess high strength and high ductility, which have potential industrial applications. The present study focuses on Al0.7CoCrFeNi, a lamellar dual-phase (fcc + B2) precipitation-strengthenable eutectic high entropy alloy. This alloy exhibits an fcc + B2 (B2 with bcc nano-precipitates) microstructure resulting in a combination of the soft and ductile fcc phase together with hard B2 phase. Low temperature annealing leads to the precipitation of ordered L12 intermetallic precipitates within the fcc resulting in enhanced strength. The strengthening contribution due to fine scale L12 is modeled using Orowan dislocation bowing and by-pass mechanism. The alloy was tested under quasi-static (strain-rate = 10−3 s−1) tensile loading and dynamic (strain-rate = 103 s−1) compressive loading. Due to the fine lamellar microstructure with a large number of fcc-bcc interfaces, the alloy show relatively high flow-stresses, ~1400 MPa under quasi-static loading and in excess of 1800 MPa under dynamic loading. The present study focuses on the marginally hypo-eutectic HEA with the nominal composition of Al0.7CoCrFeNi (15 at. % Al and 21.25 at.% each of Co, Cr, Fe, Ni). While a few previous investigations on this HEA have reported a lamellar two-phase fcc/B2microstructure in this alloy, a detailed investigation of the microstructure of this alloy and its evolution during post-solidification thermo-mechanical processing forms the basis of the present study.
